why: Splitting vertices into two groups with every edge crossing is two-colouring the graph. BFS colouring each component either succeeds or finds an edge between same-coloured vertices (an odd cycle).
hints: Two groups with every edge crossing between them: try painting vertices with two colours so that neighbours always differ.
Colour a start vertex 0, give its neighbours 1, their neighbours 0, and so on. A conflict (an edge whose ends share a colour) means not bipartite; it happens exactly when there is an odd cycle.
Build an undirected adjacency list using edges[i][j] or edges[j][i], then BFS-colour from every uncoloured vertex. O(n^2) for the matrix scan.
pitfalls: The matrix may record an edge in only one triangle; treat edges[i][j] == 1 or edges[j][i] == 1 as an edge, or a triangle stored one-sided looks bipartite.
The graph can be disconnected; start a new colouring from every uncoloured vertex, including isolated ones.
